This market will resolve according to the name of the first named storm categorized as a hurricane in the Atlantic from the creation of this market through November 30, 2026 11:59:59 PM ET. If there is no storm categorized as a hurricane in the Atlantic between market creation through November 30, 2026 11:59:59 PM ET, then this market resolves to "Other".

A hurricane is a tropical cyclone with maximum sustained winds of 74 mph or greater (Category 1 or higher on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale), as described at https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/aboutsshws.php. A tropical storm will not qualify as a hurricane even if it is named.

All names are from the NHC list of 2026 Atlantic Names (https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/aboutnames.shtml).

This market may resolve based on the initial NHC advisory reporting a qualifying hurricane regardless of any later advisory, retraction, best-track revision, or reanalysis that revises that storm's intensity downward.

eventMetadata.context_description: The alphabetical ordering of the 2026 Atlantic name list—following the recent formation of Tropical Storm Cristobal—places Dolly as the leading candidate for the season’s first hurricane, with subsequent names like Gonzalo, Edouard, and Fay reflecting the order in which later storms could intensify. A below-normal outlook from NOAA, citing suppressed activity through mid-August with only three tropical storms recorded and zero hurricanes, has kept early intensification probabilities modest. Traders weigh the climatological peak in September, when warmer sea surface temperatures and reduced wind shear often favor rapid strengthening, against the current El Niño-influenced conditions that have limited development so far. Updated National Hurricane Center model runs and the next 48-hour tropical weather outlook will provide key signals for shifts in these implied probabilities.

markets_scanned.question: Will the highest temperature in Busan be 25°C on August 16?

raw.question: Will the highest temperature in Busan be 25°C on August 16?
raw.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Gimhae Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 16 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Gimhae Intl Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/kr/busan/RKPK.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent KMA forecasts for Busan on August 16 point to a maximum near 30°C under mostly cloudy skies with 60% rain probability, moderating typical mid-August highs of 29–31°C driven by East Asian monsoon humidity and warm southerly flow. Model consensus emphasizes afternoon showers and reduced insolation as key cooling factors, narrowing the likely peak range to 26–28°C and aligning with the market's heaviest weighting on those outcomes. Historical August baselines show daily highs averaging near 30°C, yet coastal marine effects and variable precipitation introduce uncertainty that traders are pricing through real-capital bets ahead of final observational data from official stations.
